topic: Class Templates with Default Template Parameters
explanation: In C++, class templates allow the creation of generic classes that can operate with any data type. Default template parameters enable specifying default types for template parameters, simplifying class instantiation when the default suffices. This feature enhances code reusability and flexibility, especially in the context of the Standard Template Library (STL), where container classes like std::basic_ifstream use default template parameters for traits and character types.
syntax: template <class T, class U = DefaultType> class ClassName { /* ... */ };

When instantiated with 'char', it automatically uses 'std::char_traits<char>' as the default for 'Traits'. This demonstrates how default template parameters simplify class instantiation and promote code reuse in modern C++, especially within the context of the STL and its generic programming paradigm.
